status: proposed workflow contract; documentation, not an executable scheduler
purpose: Require explicit remote-author / local-operator / remote-review handoffs with reproducible commands and no implicit authority.
precedence: Repository AGENTS.md, PROJECT_SPINE.md, active reviewed artifacts and task-specific playbooks control project scope.
This contract controls handoff presentation and local operator commands; it does not grant permission to modify product requirements or close gates.

does: Read current canonical Git HEAD, AGENTS.md, PROJECT_SPINE.md and task-specific receipts before writing.
Author/review changes in the connected remote repository when the GitHub connector is available, checking final remote HEAD.
Select the smallest next authorized task from the latest review receipt and current spine.
Give runnable pull, inspect, run, select-stage, commit and push commands using exact paths and names for the CURRENT task.
When user says pushed, fetch remote HEAD and inspect the new committed artifacts before deciding the next action.
Distinguish outer-shell launches from current-agent direct execution; a rendered prompt is not execution.
never: Claim to have run user's local compiler, test suite, Codex or hardware unless actually executed with evidence.
Claim a green test, a hash match, host success, model theorem or favorable review discharges a VO or proves target qualification.
Assume user executed tests merely because artifacts were pushed.
Change accepted AS/AP/F/CON/DE, architecture, VO/AD or problem scope without exact authority.
Create an invented target, sample rate, watchdog, ISR/RTOS topology or acceptance threshold.
Offer async future work without a scheduled task.
Tell user to manually copy assistant-authored source edits if connected GitHub write access already permits committing the changes.

does: Pull assistant-authored repository changes into their local checkout.
Run local tests, builds, simulations, deterministic tasks and independent Codex reviews.
Inspect output and stage only relevant versioned reports/manifests/receipts.
Commit and push reviewed outputs to the canonical repository.
Report errors, shell exit codes or the word pushed to trigger assistant inspection.
does_not_have_to: Manually author a patch already committed by the assistant.
Publish private raw logs, binary artifacts, secrets or ignored runs directories to GitHub.

read_first: theory_of_operation.md when architecture or gates change

phases.name: REMOTE_AUTHOR
steps: Inspect current remote HEAD and the exact next gate.
Author and commit narrowly scoped code/docs/manifests to canonical GitHub, or report that no remote write tool is available.
Verify resulting remote commit SHA and relevant paths.
Issue an exact local pull-and-run handoff. If only documentation was committed, say no run/commit/push is necessary.

phases.name: LOCAL_PULL_INSPECT
steps: Check local branch and git status before pulling; never silently stash, reset or force-push unrelated work.
Pull only with git pull --ff-only origin main.
If divergent history or local tracked changes prevent the pull, STOP and report git status/branch; do not discard changes.
Validate the task manifest using tools/task.py inspect BEFORE tools/task.py run.
Capture Python exit codes without auto-closing the interactive shell.

phases.name: LOCAL_RUN
steps: Run exactly the current authorized task or collector, using quoted paths.
Run prescribed unit tests/structural checks and report which were actually executed.
Inspect stdout/stderr, produced artifacts, receipt and Engineering Briefing; distinguish good negative controls from unexpected failures.
On a nonzero exit, STOP any automatic next stage or approval and report the exact error; retain relevant diagnostic artifacts locally.
Independent review runs only after a reviewable submission and correct registered gate. Route receipts with next_task.py only when a unique permissible transition exists.
If work is performed by an already-active Codex agent, use task.py render and follow the rendered task in that invocation; do not start nested Codex via task.py run.

phases.name: LOCAL_STAGE_COMMIT_PUSH
steps: Stage ONLY the actual output manifest(s), review reports, source evidence summaries or other requested versioned artifacts.
Never use git add -A or git add . as a default.
Do not stage runs/, local binaries, private logs, .env, .venv or secrets.
Show git diff --cached --check, --stat and full git diff --cached for inspection.
If there are no staged changes, skip commit/push and report the absence of outputs.
After successful review/inspection, commit with a gate-specific message and git push origin main.
When done, tell assistant pushed or send the commit SHA.

phases.name: REMOTE_REVIEW_RESUME
steps: Fetch the remote HEAD and inspect EXACT changed files and review outcomes.
Accept review dispositions as scoped gate results, not product verification.
For REVISE/UNRESOLVED, address the precise blocker in a new versioned artifact before re-review.
For favorable review, route ONLY the next eligible operation permitted by the receipt and current policy.
Checkpoint project spine when useful; issue the next complete pull-run-push handoff with no placeholders.

shell_rules.command_block_policy: Provide COMPLETE self-contained runnable blocks for the current task. Define variables in the same block as their use, or explicitly instruct to run all blocks in the same shell.
shell_rules.avoid: Do not prepend set -euo pipefail to interactive troubleshooting commands because the shell may exit on normal task validation failure.
diagnostic_pattern: if [ "$rc" -ne 0 ]; then printf 'STOP: inspect failed; do not run or push a favorable receipt\n'; fi
stage_and_publish_example: if ! git diff --cached --quiet; then git commit -m "Independently review EXACT gate"; git push origin main; fi
shell_rules.templates_are_not_ready_to_run: Tokens such as EXACT-ID/PATH/EXACT-REPORT are INTERNAL protocol illustrations. A live assistant MUST replace them with known paths in the actual response; if paths are not yet known, provide a safe command to discover them and verify first.

failure_handling.validation_or_nonzero: Stop progression; keep Bash alive with set +e and inspect the actual return code/output.
failure_handling.already_planned: Use the existing manifest path and verify its task ID. Do not regenerate a new task unnecessarily.
failure_handling.already_present: Inspect its receipt, source fingerprints and exact input before reusing. Do not overwrite accepted versioned output.
failure_handling.no_valid_transition: Do not invent a next manifest, operation or acceptance.
failure_handling.push_conflict: Fetch current HEAD, inspect competing changes and reconcile without force.
failure_handling.unavailable_tools: State limitation and deliver an exact versioned patch or safe alternative; do not claim a remote commit succeeded.

always_include_for_local_handoff: Verified remote commit SHA and concise change summary.
Exactly named, executable git pull command.
Exact inspect/test/run commands for next authorized operation.
Output paths and expected artifact classes, explicitly labeling expectations as unverified until run.
Selective staging, inspect, commit and git push commands when local output is expected.
Stop criteria and critical remaining VOs/unknowns.
after_user_says_pushed: Do not ask for logs or SHA if remote commit is accessible.
Fetch latest remote HEAD and review newly committed evidence; if only summarized evidence is present, say so.
Follow authorized next gate, never assume cleanroom/product readiness.
response_contract.style: Concise explanation plus ready-to-paste Bash blocks; no procedural essays replacing commands.
response_contract.transparency: Always distinguish authored, generated, compiled, executed, independently reviewed, accepted scope, and product qualified.

exact_current_example.caveat: These outputs are not yet verified on remote main as of the referenced commit. Run locally and check actual files before staging.

outer_shell_launch.when: Human has a functioning Codex CLI and task starts outside an existing Codex agent session.
outer_shell_launch.evidence: Check registered runner telemetry, completed turns, exit code and actual review outputs. Exit code alone is not an authority decision.

current_agent_direct.when: Task is already assigned to an active Codex agent invocation, or nested launching is unavailable.
current_agent_direct.execute: Read and carry out the rendered prompt and playbook IN THE CURRENT agent invocation. Do not recursively call task.py run.
current_agent_direct.evidence: Explicit DIRECT_IN_CURRENT_INVOCATION identity with performed checks and versioned receipt. Never label as a successful task.py run.

execution_modes.operational_rule: Selected mode and evidence must be explicit; a failed nested launcher is not automatically cured by a direct report. Retain its failure provenance.
